content.user_title: Choose the Right Matt Pocock Skill
content.value_statement: Engineering teams often lose time choosing the next AI coding workflow. This skill routes each situation to the right Matt Pocock skill and flow.
actual_capabilities: Maps feature ideas to the main idea-to-ship flow.
Explains when to use planning, issue splitting, implementation, testing, and review skills.
Routes bug reports and incoming requests through triage or diagnosis paths.
Identifies standalone skills for research, teaching, prototyping, and skill writing.
Gives context hygiene guidance for long AI coding sessions.
limitations: Requires the referenced Matt Pocock skills to be available in the environment.
Does not implement code, run tests, or manage issues by itself.
Assumes the repository follows the workflow conventions described by the skill set.
Does not verify whether external references are current.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Flow
use_cases.description: Select the right sequence for turning a feature idea into scoped work and implementation steps.

use_cases.title: Route Incoming Work
use_cases.description: Decide whether bug reports, feature requests, or broken behavior need triage, diagnosis, or implementation.

use_cases.title: Manage Long AI Sessions
use_cases.description: Choose when to keep context, hand off work, start fresh, or compact a conversation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Point
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner routing for a simple situation.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this situation: [describe your work]. Which Matt Pocock skill should I use first, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature planning with an existing codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a feature idea in an existing codebase: [describe idea]. Route me through the correct skill flow from planning to implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Bug or Request Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: I have these incoming items: [list bugs and requests]. Tell me which items need triage, diagnosis, or direct implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Session Build
prompt_templates.prompt: This build may take several sessions: [describe scope]. Recommend the flow, handoff points, and context boundaries.

output_examples.input: I have a vague feature idea in a codebase.
output: Start with /grill-with-docs to sharpen the idea and preserve project context.
Move to /to-prd and /to-issues if the work needs multiple sessions.

output_examples.input: Users reported several unrelated bugs and feature requests.
output: Use /triage for incoming reports that need classification and shaping.
Use /diagnosing-bugs for a specific broken behavior that needs a tight feedback loop.
Avoid triaging issues already created by /to-issues.

output_examples.input: My context window is getting large before issue creation.
output: Keep the planning phase in one context window when possible.
Use /handoff if the session is degraded before /to-issues.
Continue from the handoff file in a fresh session.

best_practices: Describe your current situation before asking for a route.
Keep planning context together until the work is split into issues.
Start a fresh session for each independent implementation issue.
anti_patterns: Using /implement before the idea has been clarified enough.
Triaging issues that were already generated from a PRD.
Compacting or clearing context in the middle of a planning phase.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps choose the right Matt Pocock skill or workflow for the current engineering situation.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It routes you to other skills that can plan, implement, test, or review work.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it first?
faq.answer: Use it when you know your situation but do not know which workflow should start.

faq.question: Does it require a codebase?
faq.answer: Some recommended paths require a codebase. The skill also names standalone paths for work without one.

faq.question: Is there any security-sensitive behavior?
faq.answer: No executable behavior was found. The flagged items are Markdown slash-command names and one documentation link.
